SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part2.question: Does softness belong only to the falling body?
SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part2.ontology: A deformation encounter depends on body shape,material parameters,contact geometry and the conditions of release.
SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part2.experiment: Compare the labelled Bouncy Collider and Slippery Collider stations,then a torus or corner-strike specimen. Look for what the setup changes before explaining the resulting pose.
SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part2.observe: Different contact arrangements produce different motions and settled shapes; labels identify the intended comparison.
SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part2.limit: This is not a controlled single-variable series: some neighbours change several properties. A label describes configuration,not a measured result.
SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part2.variation: Proposed extension: Select two stations with the same body and release,changing only collider friction,then preserve their starting pose as a reference.
SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part2.handoff: A useful extension would pair identical bodies with the same release and vary only collider friction. Preserve a small witness of the starting pose so visitors can check the comparison. The next room asks about another condition that changes the result: the moment at which an experiment is stopped, and what stopping actually does.

SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics.question: If a body stops changing, has it reached equilibrium or has somebody stopped the experiment?
SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics.ontology: A simulation state and the decision to halt or heavily damp its updates are distinct.
SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics.experiment: Compare the four soft bodies and their remaining motion; look for differences between forms arrested at different times.
SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics.observe: Four bodies are released in a2×2 arrangement and receive stopping interventions on separate timers.
SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics.limit: This is not a pinned cloth sheet,despite the room title. Heavy damping and changed stiffness do not constitute an exact snapshot or evidence of natural rest.
SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics.variation: Proposed extension: Restore a real pinned cloth comparison here,or add a clock and start-pose witness to distinguish stopping a simulation from material relaxation.
SoftBodies_Cloth_Physics.handoff: For now, keep your explanation close to the four bodies you can inspect. The next room adds diagnostic colours and controls, asking how a measurement can help you distinguish changes that a silhouette alone leaves ambiguous.
open_questions: The room contains timed soft-body stopping rather than pinned cloth. Inspect history for the intended sheet, then restore it or build a sheet with visible supports and a controlled release.

SoftBodies_Playground_of_Joy.question: When the shape yields, what does its colour tell you?
SoftBodies_Playground_of_Joy.ontology: A measurement overlay expresses a chosen quantity about deformation; the same body can support several readings.
SoftBodies_Playground_of_Joy.experiment: Compare the resting outline with the changing heatmap; use MODE to compare strain,collision andvolume readings,then vary STIFFNESS while leaving other controls alone.
SoftBodies_Playground_of_Joy.observe: The specimen deforms while overlays and labels emphasise different aspects of its state.
SoftBodies_Playground_of_Joy.limit: Colour is a selected diagnostic,not pain or permanent damage. Changing stiffness also changes the numerical scale used in the energy-like display,so redness is not a fair cross-setting absolute measure.

SoftBodies_Playground_of_Joy.handoff: The following room turns towards the language of being affected. Carry this precision with you: the measured displacement is available to inspect, while the meaning assigned to it needs its own argument.

ProceduralGeneration_Reaction_Diffusion_.question: Can a pattern form without anybody drawing its outline?
ProceduralGeneration_Reaction_Diffusion_.ontology: A reaction-diffusion system stores concentrations,local reactions and spatial exchange; a visible image reads one field.
ProceduralGeneration_Reaction_Diffusion_.experiment: Select a preset,watch patches develop,then move FEED slightly while keeping KILL fixed. Use RESET to begin a new run.
ProceduralGeneration_Reaction_Diffusion_.observe: Spots,stripes or connected regions change as the concentration field evolves; the image need not follow the hand directly.
ProceduralGeneration_Reaction_Diffusion_.limit: Preset names describe a tendency,not a guaranteed biological form. Reset seeding and elapsed evolution also affect the picture.
ProceduralGeneration_Reaction_Diffusion_.variation: Proposed extension: Keep a seed and initial field fixed across paired feed settings; let one visitor disturb a region and another decide what counts as the same pattern.
ProceduralGeneration_Reaction_Diffusion_.handoff: Next, a field will become a surface with openings. Keep the distinction between the values being calculated and the visible form chosen to represent them.

Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis.question: Which openings connect inside a surface that seems to fold through itself?
Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis.ontology: An implicit surface is selected from a scalar field by a threshold; its geometry can change when field parameters change.
Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis.experiment: Follow an opening with your eye,then move to another viewpoint to test whether two apparent passages connect.
Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis.observe: The current specimen is a gyroid-like porous structure with noise perturbation.
Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis.limit: S is an authored morphing control,not measured thermodynamic entropy. One frozen specimen cannot show the effect of changing three coupled parameters.
Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis.variation: Proposed extension: Compare fixed-seed specimens varying only threshold,then onlyfrequency,before offering a combined morphing axis.
Topology_Entropy_Morphogenesis.handoff: The next sequence begins with that separation. A scalar field supplies values, a chosen level supplies a question, and an extraction procedure supplies the surface you can see. Your first task will be to locate the boundary before learning how its small pieces are made.
